name: Amp

surfaces.label: Amp CLI, interactive TUI (native Bun binary named amp; one process can host several threads)

amp --execute: one-shot headless turn (docs: sends the message, waits for the turn to end, prints the answer, exits). The probe has no per-surface signal, so it is classified by the row-level working_signals like the others
amp -x: short form of --execute (same caveat). `amp -ox` (execute in an orb) matches the interactive surface instead, because the argument is -ox, not -x
amp --no-tui runner: serves threads started from ampcode.com or the apps; the Mac app starts it as `amp --no-tui --no-serve-cwd --runner-id <mac-name>-amp-app` in the home folder

Amp for macOS (beta, macOS 26+): WebKit client, /Applications/Amp.app/Contents/MacOS/Amp. It does not run the agent itself. Deliberately no process spec: matching it would swallow its child runner and report a permanent idle row.
Orbs (per-thread cloud machines), ampcode.com web, iOS and iPadOS app: nothing runs on this Mac

working_signals.name: bash
working_signals.meaning: The agent shell tool spawns `/bin/bash -c <cmd>` (falls back to /usr/bin/bash, then /bin/sh) as a direct child of the amp process, with env AGENT=amp, AI_AGENT=amp, AGENT_THREAD_ID and AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID set. Commands the human types into the TUI use $SHELL instead (usually zsh), so they are not seen by this signal. Precise while a tool call runs, blind during model streaming and thinking. The plugin runtime is a child named amp (the same binary re-run with BUN_BE_BUN=1), not bash. A stdio MCP server configured as `bash ...` would be a persistent bash child and would make this signal stick on.

Inferred, not measured: no Amp process was available to calibrate, and 5 percent is a guess. The TUI is a Bun app that presumably animates while the agent works. Amp holds no per-turn power assertion (no caffeinate or IOKit string in the binary) and writes no local transcript, so CPU is the only whole-turn signal from outside.

waiting_signals.name: afplay
waiting_signals.meaning: The TUI plays Ping when the agent enters awaiting_approval (blocked on the human). It runs it through child_process.exec, so a short-lived `sh -c afplay ...` wrapper may sit between amp and afplay. Ping.aiff is 1.5 s long. Only when amp.notifications.enabled is true (default), the terminal has reported focus loss (amp assumes it is focused until the terminal sends a focus-out event, so a terminal without focus reporting presumably never triggers it), and at most once per 2 s. Over SSH or with AMP_FORCE_BEL it writes a BEL instead and nothing is spawned.

waiting_signals.name: afplay
waiting_signals.meaning: Turn finished, agent idle and waiting for the next message (Glass.aiff is the idle-review variant). Same conditions as Ping. Useful as a turn-ended edge, not as a level.

In-process only: ThreadState is idle | running | awaiting-approval | error (internal agentLoopState awaiting_approval). Visible to a plugin via amp.activeThread / thread.state, not from outside the process.

hooks.config: No hook config file. TypeScript or JavaScript plugins exporting a default function(amp): .amp/plugins/ in the project, ~/.config/amp/plugins/ (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/amp/plugins/) on the machine, plus personal and workspace plugins managed on ampcode.com. `amp plugins list` shows loaded plugins; `amp plugins add <url>` installs one.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry export found. The CLI binary bundles only @opentelemetry/api (trace context, used for the plugin logger's span events); it contains no OTLP exporter and never reads OTEL_EXPORTER_* variables. Amp sends its own telemetry: the binary POSTs event batches to <server>/api/telemetry. Session data is server-side; the closest local signals are ~/.cache/amp/logs/cli.log and, for execute and headless runs, ~/.cache/amp/logs/threads/<T-id>.log.

notes: No Amp process was available on this Mac, so nothing was classified live; confidence is documented, not verified-locally. Session model: the transcript lives on Amp's servers (Rivet thread-actors over WebSocket); there is no local transcript to tail, so transcript_write is not a signal and session_store is omitted on purpose. One interactive amp process can host several threads, and interactive amp takes no session id flag (`amp threads continue T-...` takes it positionally), so process to thread mapping is only possible from the env of a running bash tool child (AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID). Matching: ps shows the process as `amp` (argv[0] as typed). Every path_contains entry is redundant with names (basename amp); the ~/.amp/bin/amp entry was removed on verification because it is a substring of the Amp Desktop Helper path and made that launchd-parented helper show up as an idle TUI row. Name matching is case-sensitive: the Mac app executable is `Amp`, the CLI is `amp`, and the Objective-C detector must not fold case. Known false positives that the row format cannot remove: any other program named amp (homebrew-core's `amp` is a terminal text editor, https://amp.rs) matches by name and shows as an idle TUI row; short-lived non-interactive subcommands not in exclude_args (amp threads list, amp mcp ..., amp usage ...) show as idle TUI rows while they run; `amp -ox` (execute in an orb) matches the interactive surface. Process tree: the plugin runtime is the amp binary re-run with BUN_BE_BUN=1, so an amp process can have amp children; the probe keeps the outermost. Stdio MCP servers are also persistent children of an idle amp, so do not treat 'any child' as working. The Mac app is a client: the agent runs in an orb or in the `amp --no-tui` runner child, which uses the amp found on the login-shell PATH. Amp Desktop Helper.app (~/.amp/bin/amp-desktop-helper/<version>) exists only for `amp --no-tui --desktop`. The execute surfaces are labels only: the probe applies row-level signals to every surface. Nothing here was checked against a live process; first live run should confirm the process name, the bash child, the afplay child, and the CPU floor.
